scenes.title: Talavera
scenes.subject: A Talavera pottery workshop in Puebla, Mexico, medium shot: a smiling Mexican woman artisan in a simple apron sits at a wooden worktable and hand-paints a large round white tin-glazed plate with a fine brush, drawing an intricate cobalt-blue floral pattern with touches of yellow and orange; behind her, wooden shelves full of finished Talavera plates, tiles, jars and vases in cobalt blue, yellow, orange and green on glossy white glaze. Warm daylight from a window.
scenes.motion: The artisan paints steady blue brushstrokes on the plate, dips her brush in the cobalt paint and turns the plate on the table to keep painting; she smiles; the camera slowly pushes in.

scenes.title: Barro Negro
scenes.subject: A barro negro pottery workshop in San Bartolo Coyotepec, Oaxaca, medium shot: an older Zapotec woman artisan with grey braids, a white embroidered blouse and an apron sits on a low stool and polishes a round unfired grey clay pot (cántaro) held on her lap by rubbing it with a smooth quartz stone; beside her on a table stand finished barro negro pieces, glossy jet-black clay pots, jars and openwork lamps with a metallic shine, lit by warm light.
scenes.motion: The artisan rubs the quartz stone over the pot in steady circles, turning the pot slowly on her lap as its surface begins to shine; she looks up and smiles.

scenes.title: Árbol de la Vida
scenes.subject: A clay workshop in Metepec, State of Mexico, medium shot: a smiling Mexican artisan carefully paints a large Árbol de la Vida (tree of life) clay sculpture, a candelabra-shaped tree densely covered with small clay flowers, leaves, doves and little figures, painted in vivid pink, yellow, turquoise, green, orange and red; pots of bright paint and brushes on the table; other painted trees of life on shelves behind.
scenes.motion: The artisan paints small clay flowers on the tree of life with a fine brush, dipping it in the paint pots and dabbing colour onto one flower after another; she smiles and leans in. The tree of life stays completely still and unchanged in place; nobody turns or moves it; only the artisan's hands and brush move. Only one person in the scene.

scenes.title: Alebrijes
scenes.subject: An alebrije workshop in San Martín Tilcajete, Oaxaca, medium shot: a smiling Zapotec artisan paints fine patterns of dots and lines in vivid colours onto a hand-carved copal-wood alebrije, a fantastical jaguar-dragon with wings; finished brightly patterned alebrijes (a fox, a cat, a winged lizard) stand on the table around jars of paint; his partner carves a new figure with a machete-like knife in the background.
scenes.motion: The artisan dots bright colours onto the alebrije's wing with a fine brush, dipping the brush in the paint jars and adding dot after dot; the alebrije stays still on the table and is never lifted or turned; in the background his partner shaves curls of wood from a new figure with a knife.

scenes.title: Tapetes Zapotecos
scenes.subject: A weaving workshop in Teotitlán del Valle, Oaxaca, medium shot: a smiling Zapotec weaver works at a large wooden pedal (treadle) loom, weaving a wool rug with a bold geometric Zapotec step-fret (greca) design in cochineal red, indigo blue, marigold yellow and natural cream; baskets of naturally dyed wool yarn balls and hanging skeins in red, blue, yellow and brown beside the loom.
scenes.motion: The weaver presses the pedals, passes the wooden shuttle through the threads with one hand and pulls the beater toward him to pack the row, again and again in a steady rhythm; the loom's threads move up and down.

scenes.title: Arte Huichol
scenes.subject: A Wixárika (Huichol) artisan from the Sierra Madre in Jalisco, medium close shot: a smiling young woman wearing a white cotton blouse embroidered with colourful Huichol motifs and many beaded bracelets presses tiny colourful glass beads one by one into a layer of beeswax covering a carved wooden jaguar head, creating a dazzling pattern of flowers, deer and peyote motifs in bright turquoise, yellow, red, magenta and blue; small bowls of loose beads on the table.
scenes.motion: With a fine needle the artisan picks up tiny beads and presses them into the wax one after another, adding to the bright pattern; she turns the beaded jaguar head to show it and smiles.

scenes.title: Papel Picado
scenes.subject: A papel picado workshop in San Salvador Huixcolotla, Puebla, medium shot: a smiling Mexican artisan cuts a thick stack of brightly coloured tissue paper with a small hammer and a metal chisel, tapping out an intricate pattern; strings of finished papel picado banners in pink, orange, green, purple, yellow and turquoise with cut-out flowers and birds hang across the workshop behind him.
scenes.motion: The artisan taps the chisel with the hammer in quick strikes, moving along the pattern; then he lifts the top sheet and it unfolds into a lacy pink banner; the hanging banners flutter in a breeze.

scenes.title: Piñatas
scenes.subject: A piñata workshop in Acolman, State of Mexico, medium shot: a smiling Mexican woman artisan decorates a large seven-point star piñata, gluing frills of brightly coloured fringed tissue paper onto its cones; finished star piñatas in pink, orange, purple, silver and gold with long tissue-paper streamers hang from the ceiling behind her.
scenes.motion: The artisan wraps and presses a strip of fringed tissue paper around a cone, fluffs the fringe with her fingers and turns the piñata to the next cone; the hanging piñatas sway gently and their streamers flutter.

scenes.title: Cartonería
scenes.subject: A cartonería (papier-mâché) workshop in Mexico City, medium shot: a smiling Mexican artisan paints a tall papier-mâché La Catrina figure, an elegant skeleton lady with a wide flowered hat and a long colourful dress, adding bright flower details to her painted skull face; colourful cartonería alebrijes and Judas figures stand around the workshop.
scenes.motion: The artisan paints a flower on the Catrina's hat with careful brushstrokes, dips his brush and adds bright dots to her dress, then steps back a little and smiles at his work. The Catrina figure stays completely still and unchanged in place; nobody turns or moves it.

scenes.title: Plata de Taxco
scenes.subject: A silversmith's workshop in Taxco, Guerrero, medium close shot: a Mexican silversmith in a leather apron hammers a gleaming sterling silver cuff bracelet on a small steel mandrel at his workbench, giving it a hammered texture; finished shining silver jewellery (necklaces, earrings, bracelets with turquoise) lies on a velvet cloth; through the window the white houses and red roofs of hillside Taxco.
scenes.motion: The silversmith taps the silver bracelet with a small hammer in a quick steady rhythm, turning it on the mandrel; the silver glints and flashes with each strike; he holds it up to the light and smiles.

scenes.title: Cobre Martillado
scenes.subject: A coppersmith workshop in Santa Clara del Cobre, Michoacán, medium shot: two Purépecha coppersmiths in work clothes hammer a large glowing orange-hot copper vessel on an anvil, a forge with burning coals behind them; finished hammered copper pots, vases and plates with shining reddish-gold surfaces line the walls.
scenes.motion: The two coppersmiths strike the glowing copper vessel with their hammers in turn, a steady alternating rhythm, rotating it on the anvil; sparks fly and the forge's coals glow and flicker.

scenes.title: Vidrio Soplado
scenes.subject: A hand-blown glass workshop in Tlaquepaque, Jalisco, medium shot: a Mexican glassblower turns a long metal blowpipe with a glowing orange gather of molten glass at its end in front of a roaring furnace, blowing into it to shape a bubble; finished hand-blown glasses, jugs and vases with bright cobalt-blue rims and small bubbles in the glass stand on shelves.
scenes.motion: The glassblower blows into the pipe while rolling it, and the glowing glass bubble swells; he turns it in the fire and shapes it with a wet wooden paddle as it glows brighter; the furnace roars.
